Barbarian · Theorycraft

Ravenous Rend Wave Barbarian

rend-stacking bleed

Barbarian theorycraft unchanged rend-stacking bleed confidence low PTR

Last verified 2026-08-09 • Season 15 (PTR)

PTR - subject to change before Season 15 launches; this is untested theorycraft resting on 3.2.0 PTR values that may be revised. It is deliberately a contrarian build. Every source says Barbarian bleed was nerfed in 3.2.0, and they are right about the headline: Two-Handed Sword Expertise's bleeding bonus was halved from 30%[x] to 15%[x] and the Hemorrhage node went 75%[x] to 60%[x]. But Ring of the Ravenous was not simply nerfed, it was reworked - its duration and damage came down (6-8s to 4-6s, 60-80% to 40-60%) while it gained the ability to apply a Rend stack and had its cooldown halved from 1 second to 0.5. A shorter, weaker, twice-as-frequent effect that also applies stacks is a different item, not a worse one. The hypothesis is that Rend-stack application rate now matters more than per-stack magnitude, which would make a fast-hitting Rend build better than the raw numbers suggest. Honest framing: no source supports this, the consensus reading is that Barbarian bleed is dead, and this build exists to test whether the consensus read the rework as a nerf without checking the cooldown line.

Requirements

  • Ring of the Ravenousring
  • Tuskhelm of Joritz the Mightyhelm
  • Tibault's Willpants
  • Nomad's Longing Heartamulet
  • SSplinter of Hellfirejewelry socket
  • Rage of Harrogath
  • Shattered Vowoffhand
Stage
Move on whenLevel 70, Torment 1, and Ring of the Ravenous in hand. Run the stack-counting test in test_notes the moment you equip it, before investing further.
Move on whenThe stack-count test has passed - roughly double application rate confirmed, and Rend damage confirmed to scale per stack rather than merely refresh. If either check fails, stop and play barbarian-meta-upheaval-red-furor instead. That is not a fallback, it is the correct answer to a failed hypothesis.
Move on whenThis build only graduates to pushing if it has beaten barbarian-meta-upheaval-red-furor in a direct comparison at equal gear. If it merely competes, report that as the finding and push the meta build instead.

Rend15/15

[ptr] Provenance, stated plainly. No 3.2.0 skill tree is published for any build on any site - the official notes carry no allocations, and Maxroll, Icy Veins, d4builds and d4guides were all still serving Season 14 guides on 2026-08-08, day 5 of the 8-day PTR. This allocation is therefore the specialist's, built from the skill list the PTR digest authorises for this class plus the 3.2.0 changes that actually apply. Treat the point counts as a starting shape to test, not as a published build. Where a skill's upgrade mods are named below, those names are carried over from Season 14 planner data - 3.2.0 does not rename them. Where a skill appears with no mods, that is deliberate: its mod names were not published anywhere consulted, and inventing them would be worse than leaving them out. On the PTR you can skip this stage outright - Mrak's boosts grant level 70 and maxed aspects directly - so this allocation is written for what a live Season 15 would look like.

War Cry15/15
Challenging Shout15/15
Lunging Strike7/15
LSkewer1/3
Berserking1/3
Leap1/15
Earthshatter1/3
Fury Generation1/3
Wrath of the Berserker5/15

Skill point priority

  1. Rend to max - the build is an application-rate experiment and Rend is what gets applied
  2. Lunging Strike for Fury generation, still capped at 0.5 Fury per 1% Maximum Life since 3.1.x
  3. War Cry for Berserking and Vulnerable
  4. Challenging Shout for damage reduction - a melee bleed build on a class that lost 27% of its baseline scaling needs it
  5. Leap for gap closing
  6. Wrath of the Berserker as the ultimate for its flat +30% all damage

Skill bar

1Lunging Strike
2Rend
3War Cry
4Challenging Shout
5Rallying Cry
6Wrath of the Berserker

Rotation

Shouts up, Lunging Strike to sustain Fury, Rend continuously rather than in bursts - the whole point is application frequency. Ring of the Ravenous is now on a 0.5 second cooldown instead of 1 second, so the correct rhythm is faster and shallower than Season 14 Rend play. Count stacks; this stage is data collection.

Rotation

Untested at push tiers and unlikely to reach them - be blunt about that. The most probable outcome is that this hypothesis fails at test step two, because damage-over-time stacks that only refresh a duration are common in this game and the patch notes give no reason to think Rend is different. It is written out in full anyway because a rework with a halved cooldown deserves ten minutes of testing before an archetype is written off on a headline nerf, and a PTR is exactly where that ten minutes costs nothing. All values are 3.2.0 PTR values and may change before Season 15 launches.

Board & glyph focus

Attack Speed and Bleeding routes first - if the hypothesis is right, application rate is the scaling stat and attack speed buys application rate. Then survivability. Explicitly do not route through Hemorrhage or Blood Rage expecting Season 14 value: both were cut on the PTR (75%[x] to 60%[x] and 60%[x] to 45%[x]), and this build's case does not depend on them.

Board & glyph focus

Attack Speed, Bleeding and survivability routes maxed. Two hard avoids carried from the meta build. Ramaladni's Magnum Opus: on the PTR it drains 10% of Maximum Fury rather than a flat 10 per second, which punishes any build that wants a full bar to sustain a generator loop. Two-Handed Sword Expertise: its bleeding bonus was halved to 15%[x], so the Season 14 instinct to reach for a two-handed sword specifically for bleed no longer pays - pick the weapon that gives attack speed instead.

How to run them

[ptr] 3.2.0 changes nothing about mercenaries - the words "Mercenary" and "Mercenaries" and all four mercenary names are absent from the official 3.2.0 notes entirely. So this is the Season 14 pairing carried over, which is the only guidance that exists. Hire Raheir for Valiance's rotating cheat-death and Inspiration's damage multiplier, and reinforce with Varyana on Bloodthirst for attack speed. One PTR-specific point worth making: Barbarian's core stat scalar was cut 1.1 to 0.8, so the class is measurably squishier per point of Strength than it was in Season 14 - if you find yourself dying on the PTR where you did not before, swapping Varyana for Aldkin's Field of Languish is the honest response, and it is a pairing Maxroll already endorses for Barbarian.

Reasoning

HypothesisRing of the Ravenous' halved cooldown (1s to 0.5s) plus its new Rend-stack application means total Rend uptime and stack count roughly double, which more than compensates for the 25-33% cut to its own duration and damage. If Rend damage scales with stack count, a build built for application rate beats one built for per-hit magnitude even after the Two-Handed Sword Expertise bleeding cut from 30%[x] to 15%[x].
Confidencelow
How to test itConfidence is low deliberately - this contradicts every source read. Test cheaply and be willing to abandon it. (1) On a dummy, count Rend stacks applied per ten seconds with Ring of the Ravenous equipped versus not. If the halved cooldown does not translate into roughly double the application rate, the premise is wrong at step one. (2) Confirm whether Rend damage actually scales per stack or whether stacks only refresh a duration. This is the load-bearing unknown and the patch notes do not answer it - if stacks merely refresh, the whole build collapses and should be abandoned without further testing. (3) Compare total damage against barbarian-meta-upheaval-red-furor at equal gear. The meta build's Ring of Red Furor occupies the same ring slot conceptually, so this is a genuine either-or, not a complement. (4) Check whether the Scorching upgrade's new fire wave scales with Rend stacks or is a flat effect - the aggregators do not mention it at all, so this may be entirely unexplored ground or entirely worthless. (5) Watch survivability: a bleed build fights at melee range with a class that just lost 27% of its baseline scaling.

Uniques & where to find them

Ring of the Ravenousring

PTR route: PTR Boosts from the vendor Mrak next to the main Waypoint in any major city. Live route: unpublished for 3.2.0; it exists in Season 14's general unique pool, so expect a lair-boss target farm or the Horadric Cube 'Upgrade to Unique' recipe. The entire hypothesis is this item - do not attempt the build without it.

Where →
Tuskhelm of Joritz the Mightyhelm

PTR route: Mrak's PTR Boosts. Live route (Season 14, unchanged): general unique pool - lair-boss target farm or the Horadric Cube 'Upgrade to Unique' recipe on a Common helm.

Where →
Tibault's Willpants

PTR route: Mrak's PTR Boosts. Live route (Season 14, unchanged): Horadric Cube 'Upgrade to Unique' recipe on Common pants (1 Enhanced Primordial Dust and 10 Primordial Dust) rather than a dedicated boss.

Where →
Nomad's Longing Heartamulet

PTR route: Mrak's PTR Boosts. Live route: unpublished for 3.2.0. Its PTR change - double damage now includes Healthy enemies - suits a bleed build unusually well, since Rend stacks are applied at the start of a fight when everything is still healthy.

Where →
SSplinter of Hellfirejewelry socket

New Soul Splinter socketable, jewelry only. PTR route: Mrak's PTR Boosts include Soul Splinters. Live route: unpublished. This is the rare build that should genuinely consider Hellfire over Anguish: it deals 40-100% increased damage at the cost of 100% Critical Strike Chance, and if this build's damage really is dominated by Rend damage-over-time stacks rather than by critical hits, the trade is favourable. That 'if' is untested and is part of what the build is for. Verify on a dummy - compare Hellfire against Anguish directly - before committing, and expect Anguish to win if Rend turns out to crit.

Where →
Rage of Harrogath

Target-farm Duriel, King of Maggots, a Greater-tier Lair boss (1x Greater Lair Key) - the dedicated source for this item.

Where →
Shattered Vowoffhand

Mythic Unique with no dedicated boss: every Lair boss can drop it, or craft it in the Horadric Cube with Pandemonium Fragments - remembering that only one Cube-crafted Mythic may be equipped at a time.

Skill rotation

  1. Keep War Cry and Challenging Shout up, sustain Fury with Lunging Strike, and apply Rend continuously rather than in bursts.
  2. The rhythm is faster and shallower than old Rend play, because application frequency is the whole point.
